documents.title: ReAct: Synergizing Reasoning and Acting in Language Models
documents.content: ReAct interleaves reasoning traces with task-specific actions. On HotpotQA and FEVER, actions allow the model to interact with a Wikipedia API, while reasoning traces help update action plans and handle exceptions. The paper reports that ReAct improves interpretability, but prompting examples and occasional non-informative reasoning remain limitations.

documents.title: ReAct: Synergizing Reasoning and Acting in Language Models
documents.content: ReAct interleaves reasoning traces and actions within a task trajectory. It uses observations from external environments to update subsequent reasoning and actions.

documents.title: Reflexion: Language Agents with Verbal Reinforcement Learning
documents.content: Reflexion converts task feedback into verbal reflections and stores them in an episodic memory buffer for later trials. It does not update model weights, and performance depends on useful feedback and reflection quality.

documents.title: Reflexion: Language Agents with Verbal Reinforcement Learning
documents.content: Reflexion uses linguistic feedback, verbal self-reflection, and episodic memory instead of weight updates. The paper evaluates decision-making, reasoning, and programming tasks and reports improvements over baselines. Results depend on the evaluator feedback, reflection model, prompts, memory window, model version, and environment setup. Evidence locator: arXiv 2303.11366, Sections 2-4.
